chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazee' from Safwan from Musa ibn Bakr from Zurara from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The khul' (divorce initiated by the wife) does not take effect until she says: 'I will not obey you in any matter, nor will I fulfill your oath, nor will I uphold your ruling for you; so take from me and divorce me.' When she says this, it becomes permissible for him to release her (in khul') for whatever amount they mutually agree upon, whether small or large. This does not occur except in the presence of a ruler (judge). When she does this, she is more entitled to herself than others, without it being named as a talaq (husband-initiated divorce).

key_terms.الْخُلْعُ: Khul' (divorce initiated by the wife in exchange for compensation)
key_terms.طَلَاقًا: Talaq (standard divorce initiated by the husband)

ai.seo_question: What are the specific conditions and legal requirements for khul' in Shia Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-istibsar details the specific verbal formula required for khul', where the wife declares she cannot fulfill her duties, thereby granting the husband the right to release her for a mutually agreed compensation. It emphasizes that this process must occur under the authority of a judge (sultan) and clarifies that the resulting separation is distinct from standard talaq, preserving the wife's autonomy over her personhood.
